items.label: Industry: Video Games & Interactive Entertainment
items.detail: Selected from active-conviction account holdings: TTWO (Take-Two Interactive, 79 sh, $16,960.51, 3.46% of NAV) is the account's only video-game holding and, together with GOOG, makes up the account's entire Telecomm/Communication-Services sector sleeve (3.87% of NAV) -- it has never been the subject of a dedicated scout cycle, unlike the account's other names (LLY covered 2026-08-31 under GLP-1/Metabolic; CCJ/FCX/KGC/NEM/REMX covered 2026-08-31 under Critical Minerals & Precious Metals Mining; CRWV/GEV covered 2026-08-30 under AI Datacenter Power Infrastructure). The industry has also seen a landscape-altering event since the last scout cycle: Electronic Arts, one of the sector's largest public pure-plays, completed a $55B take-private by Saudi PIF/Silver Lake/Affinity Partners on 2026-08-04, removing a major public comparable right as GTA 6's reaffirmed November 19, 2026 launch approaches.

items.label: TTWO
items.detail: Existing holding, thesis reinforced with real new evidence: Take-Two/Rockstar and CEO Strauss Zelnick have reaffirmed GTA 6 will launch November 19, 2026 and 'won't be delayed again' (after two prior delays, from fall 2025 to May 2026 to November 2026); separately, EA's $55B take-private (completed 2026-08-04, $210/share cash) removes a major public AAA comparable from the market right as industry M&A hit $7.7B across 52 deals in Q1 2026 and $2.3B across 54 deals in Q2 2026, evidence that strategic and financial buyers are actively re-rating game-industry IP upward. Genuine risk: the investment case now rests heavily on single-title execution risk for a game that has already slipped twice.
items.diversification_note: TTWO is already the account's entire Telecomm/Communication-Services sector sleeve alongside GOOG (3.87% of NAV combined, $18,998.96) -- reinforcing here deepens an existing concentrated sector bet rather than diversifying it.

items.label: RBLX
items.detail: Roblox -- not currently held. The UGC/creator-economy platform posted 132M daily active users in Q1 2026 (+35% YoY) and $1.442B revenue (+39% YoY), with an all-time gaming concurrency record of 47.4M simultaneous players set August 2025 -- a structurally different growth engine than TTWO's traditional AAA publishing model. Real, unresolved overhang: 162 child-safety lawsuits have been consolidated into a single federal case with a settlement tab approaching $36M, plus an active Senate child-safety probe, even after Roblox rolled out its Sentinel real-time detection model and a rebuilt parental-control suite. Last price $43.48 (+4.75% on the day).
items.suggested_size: Modest starter given the litigation/regulatory overhang, roughly 0.5-1% of account NAV (~$2,500-$5,000).
items.diversification_note: Would land in the account's Telecomm/Communication-Services sleeve alongside TTWO and GOOG, but on a structurally different UGC-platform/creator-economy model rather than TTWO's AAA-title-driven revenue -- partial intra-sector differentiation, not true sector diversification.

items.label: U
items.detail: Unity Software -- not currently held. Functions as industry infrastructure ('picks-and-shovels') via its game engine, used across a large share of mobile and indie titles, and sits at the center of the industry's generative-AI tooling shift (28% of studios now use generative AI to draft initial game design documents, per GDC's 2026 State of the Industry survey). Trading at $41.55 (-1.26% on the day), well off prior highs after the 2023 Runtime Fee pricing fiasco damaged developer trust -- a real turnaround/re-rating candidate if new leadership executes, but Epic's free-for-most-use-cases Unreal Engine is a genuine competitive ceiling on pricing power.
items.suggested_size: Small starter tranche, roughly 0.25-0.5% of account NAV (~$1,250-$2,500); turnaround thesis carries real execution uncertainty.

items.label: UBSFY
items.detail: Ubisoft (US unsponsored ADR) -- not currently held. Tencent completed a EUR1.16B investment for a 26.32% stake in Vantage Studios, the new Ubisoft subsidiary holding the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six franchises (deal closed November 2025, EUR3.8B pre-money EV for Vantage) -- a capital-injection template that, following the EA-goes-private precedent, raises real (if unconfirmed) speculation about a fuller buyout down the line. The US ADR (UBSFY, pink sheets) last traded $1.08 (-3.87% on the day) and is thin/illiquid; worth tracking via a cleaner entry point (e.g. the primary Paris listing) rather than acting on the US ADR directly.

items.label: NTDOY
items.detail: Nintendo (US unsponsored ADR) -- not currently held. Switch 2 has sold 23.68M units through June 30, 2026 -- already exceeding the original GameCube's full lifetime total (21.74M) -- and was the fastest hardware launch in Nintendo history (3.5M units in 4 days) and fastest to 10M units (4 months); software attach rate is running roughly 2.46 games per console. Real structural hardware-cycle strength, but the only US-accessible line found (NTDOY, pink sheets, unsponsored) last traded $14.07 (-1.26% on the day) and is an illiquid ADR, not a clean proxy for the primary Tokyo listing -- flagging for a future cycle once a better-access vehicle is confirmed rather than acting today.

items.label: EU Digital Fairness Act / loot-box regulation
items.detail: No specific ticker yet, theme-level signal: the EU's Digital Fairness Act, expected as a formal proposal in Q4 2026, could ban loot boxes outright or mandate parental consent for in-game purchases by minors; separately, PEGI's March 2026 ratings overhaul already reclassifies any game with paid random items as PEGI 16+ minimum for new submissions from June 2026, and the UK's ASA has moved to active enforcement on loot-box disclosure in app-store listings. The US still has no federal loot-box law, but this is a genuine, live monetization-model risk across the live-service/free-to-play segment of the whole industry (affecting TTWO's NBA 2K and mobile titles as well as RBLX's virtual-item economy) -- carry forward to the next scout cycle for name-level follow-up as the EU proposal firms up.
